To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The structure of neocortical functional circuitry is not random, but rather exhibits non-random connections that generalize across three distinct areas of sensory cortex.

functional circuit structure is non random, that circuit size does not depend on the number of neurons sampled, and that functional circuit topology is independent of the spatial scale of the analysis.

functional circuitry exhibits a bias toward non random and occasionally long range connections, that feedforwardness is related to eigenvector centrality in all functional circuits, that circuit size does not scale with the size of the sampled neocortical population, that circuit topology is not biased by the pia, and that a minimum sample size of neurons is necessary to capture at most 90% of the circuit topology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organization of functional circuitry within the neocortex.
understanding the structure of functional circuits and the rules that govern them.
the organization of spontaneous circuit dynamics in the neocortex and how this organization relates to the underlying structure of neocortical microcircuitry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functional wiring diagrams of neocortex, at least in the mouse, have a common organization that is independent of the sensory modality.
functional circuitry is organized in a manner that is consistent with the notion that the neocortical microcircuit is a highly interconnected and dynamic network.
there are general principles of neocortical organization which are common to all cortical regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the functional circuitry of mouse neocortex is best described as an interconnected, non random network in which the temporal flow of activity is biased toward feedforward projections.

the organization of functional circuitry is best described by a non random and occasionally long distance connectivity, and that the structure of circuit topology is independent of the underlying neuronal population.

the organization of functional neocortical circuits is best described as a non-random, distal, and highly connected circuitry with a minimal bias towards feedforwardness and a maximal bias towards angular flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
functional circuit structure is not tied to sensory processing and that the organization of functional circuits can be captured by graph invariants.
the structure of functional circuitry is not random.
the organization of functional neocortical circuits is not random, and that the structure is not tied to any particular cortical region.
